title: Compiler gate policy, version 0
description: What a build is allowed to do, and what has to still be true when it finishes. Read by every component in compiler/; written by none of them.

failOn.description: Lowest severity that turns findings into exit code 2.

failOnIncomplete.description: An observation that could not be made is exit 3. Setting this false is a decision to accept unchecked builds and is recorded in the evidence.

pin.description: Path to the toolchain pin, relative to the policy file. Its digest is checked before anything is compiled.

allowedPassPlugins.description: LLVM pass plugins loadable with -fpass-plugin. A plugin not listed here is VG-PLG-002 whatever its digest.

allowedFrontendPlugins.description: Clang AST plugins loaded with -fplugin. A separate list on purpose: the two plugin mechanisms take different flags, and a check that knows only one of them passes the other straight through.

allowedPassPipeline.description: Pass pipeline the build is expected to run, as reported by the compiler. Absent means the pipeline is recorded but not constrained.

required.description: Flags that must be present in the normalised command line.

forbidden.description: Flags that must not be. A match is VG-CFG-002.

optLevels.description: Optimisation levels this policy has been evaluated at. Compiling at another one is VG-CFG-003, because a property observed to survive -O1 has not been observed to survive -O3.

properties.description: Security properties this build is required to preserve, forbid, or account for. Keys are property ids from compiler/schema/properties.json.

observeAt.description: Checkpoints at which this property is examined. A property with no reachable checkpoint is exit 3, not a pass.

artifact.description: Properties the finished binary must have. Each is decided from a structural field, never from a tool's human-readable line, and the record says which field decided it.

forbidStrings.description: Literal byte sequences that must not survive into the artefact. Compared against extracted strings; a hit is VG-ART-005.

out.description: Bundle directory. Must resolve outside compiler/.

sourceDateEpoch.description: When set, every timestamp comes from here and the record says so. Null means wall clock, also recorded.

fallback.description: Recompiling a function that lost a property, at a lower optimisation level, and checking again. Off by default: it changes what the compiler was asked to do, so it is opted into rather than applied on a checker's initiative.

profile.description: Which lower level to recompile at. "-O0" and "-O1" name it here. "auto" declines to name it and has the driver read it out of the measured table at `profileTable` instead, so that the level comes from a configuration that was observed to keep the property rather than from a guess written into a policy file. "auto" without `profileTable` is refused rather than defaulted; that pairing is checked in the driver and not in this file, because the validator in compiler/driver/lib/jsonschema.mjs implements only the keywords the rest of this schema uses and refuses the rest, so a conditional written here would fail every policy that carries a fallback block.

profileTable.description: Path to a `vgc.fallback-table/1` document, relative to this policy file. Read only when `profile` is "auto", and ignored otherwise. Each of its rows says which weaker configuration was measured to still hold one property that a stated configuration lost. Four things stop the run separately rather than being folded into one message, because they call for different work: the table cannot be read, the table was derived from an envelope that is no longer the one on disk, the table has no row for this build's configuration, and the table has a row that records no safe target. The level a row names is still only a level to try — the property is observed again after the recompile, and a property that does not come back is rejected as it was before.

exposureFrontiers.description: Path to a `vibeguard.ladder-frontiers/1` sidecar, relative to this policy file. Optional, and read only once a level has otherwise resolved from `profileTable`. It closes a hole in the six-axis key those rows are filed under: the key is nominal, and the optimiser is not. Run this driver's own `normalise` and `driverConfigAxes` over `-O2`, over `-O2 -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, over `-O2 -fno-builtin-memset` and over `-O2 -ffast-math` and the same key comes back for all four, so a row measured under plain `-O2` is quoted for builds that are not the one it was measured in. The sidecar carries, per configuration key, the graded response of a small specimen compiled separately under that key's own flags; a response measured for this build that differs from the one recorded beside the cell is evidence that at least one probed mechanism differs, and the run is refused rather than answered from that cell. A response that does not differ is `exposure-consistent`: necessary, never sufficient, and never reported as a match. Naming a sidecar here only ever refuses builds — it never fills a cell, never chooses one, and never turns a lost property into a passing build. Fail-closed: naming a sidecar refuses every fallback until a measured frontier is supplied for the build in hand — an unanswered guard is not a passed one. Two measured limits belong beside the `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3` example above, because they sit directly under the example that sells this key. On clang 18.1.3, measured 2026-08-17: `-O2`, `-O3` and `-Os` are indistinguishable to the specimen's rungs, so a sidecar entry cannot tell those three apart; and `_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2` and `=3` are indistinguishable too, so what this guard separates is FORTIFY on from FORTIFY off, not `=2` from `=3`. A build that moves only within either of those groups is a build this key does not see, and the residual hole is disclosed here rather than papered over.

name.description: Basename as loaded. Matching on the name alone is not enough — a file with this name and different bytes is a different plugin, which is why the digest is required rather than optional.
